Series is the McAlpine Locks and Dam lower (tailwater) gauge as kept by the Louisville District LPMS. The LRL location record for this series (McAlpine-MLPK2) has no coordinates; lat/lon and gauge zero come from the LRL record McAlpineLWR (Ohio River at Louisville, KY), which matches USGS 03294500.

Gauge zero 373.18 ft NGVD29 (374.00 ft on the Ohio River datum, per USGS). The gauge sits below McAlpine Locks and Dam (Locks and Dam 41 until 1960; the present dam was built in the 1960s). USGS says various combinations of gauges near Louisville were used before October 1939 and in 1943 to 1946.
Observed in the data, cause not documented: the yearly minimum rises from about 3 to 5 ft before 1923 to about 9 ft from 1923 on. Do not compare low-water readings across 1923 without checking.
Levels are rounded to 0.01 ft: the API converts from stored meters and returns float noise such as 12.979999999999999.

measurement_history.fact: USACE: the Louisville and Portland Canal opened when the first boat passed through on Dec. 22, 1830.
Earliest crest in the NWS historic crest list for the McAlpine lower gauge is Feb. 21, 1832.
USGS: gauge-height records near Louisville since 1871 are published in NWS reports.
USACE: the Louisville project became Locks and Dam 41 when lock numbering began around 1914.
USGS: before Oct. 1939 and in 1943 to 1946, various combinations of gauges near Louisville were used.
USGS used a nonrecording gauge 0.3 mile upstream at the same datum from Oct. 1946 to Sept. 1961.
USACE renamed Locks and Dam 41 as McAlpine Locks and Dam; in the 1960s the canal was widened and the present dam built.
Present gauge: water-stage recorder at the downstream end of the lock guide wall, in the lower pool of McAlpine Locks.
Gauge zero 373.18 ft NGVD29, equal to 374.00 ft on the Ohio River datum.
Date the present recorder or telemetry began: not found in USGS NWC page or NWS gauge data.

public_notes: This gauge sits in the lower pool of McAlpine Locks, so the river here is managed by locks and a dam (USGS). USGS says various combinations of gauges near Louisville were used before October 1939 and from 1943 to 1946, so readings from those years are less comparable.
